title: Waves (KS4 Physics)
subject: Physics
strapline: Transverse and longitudinal waves and the wave equation.
facts: A wave transfers energy from one place to another without transferring matter.
In a transverse wave, the vibrations are at right angles to the direction of travel (e.g. light, water ripples).
In a longitudinal wave, the vibrations are along the direction of travel, making compressions and rarefactions (e.g. sound).
Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the rest position; wavelength is the distance for one full wave.
Frequency is the number of waves per second, measured in hertz (Hz).
Wave speed = frequency × wavelength (v = f × λ).
The electromagnetic spectrum (radio, micro, infrared, visible, UV, X-ray, gamma) are all transverse and travel at the speed of light in a vacuum.

quick_quiz.q: What does a wave transfer without moving matter?
Sound is which type of wave?

teacher_tips: Demonstrate both wave types with a slinky.
Keep amplitude (height) vs wavelength (length) clearly apart.
Order the EM spectrum by increasing frequency/decreasing wavelength.
